tasks.short: Read the job's specifications, look up the setup sheet, determine the setup and select dies and parts, and record the settings used.

steps.what: Extrusion operator reads the job's specifications from the paper job sheet
Extrusion operator looks up the product's setup sheet in a binder
Extrusion operator determines setup procedures and selects machine dies and parts
Extrusion operator writes the settings used on the job sheet

tasks.design: The job, its specifications and the product's setup sheet with die and part numbers are shown on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the operator does not read a paper job sheet and search a binder. Temperatures, speeds and pressures are taken from the machine control when the run starts, and the operator notes only changes. Determining the setup and selecting dies stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications came on paper, setup sheets sat in binders and settings were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems show jobs and setup sheets at the machine and read machine data.
tasks.still_hard: Older lines have no data link to the control.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how a die behaves with a new batch of material.

reach.learn: Whether settings per run are complete.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X Machine Monitoring collects produced quantities and machine statuses from the machine control or by manual entry.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new job to settings recorded; product design is outside.
Input contract: setup sheets loaded per product; fallback is the binder.
Setup decisions stay with the operator.
Works council consent comes before machine data are tied to logins.

incremental.description: Extrusion operator reports outdated setup sheets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older lines without data links; high: connected lines with many product changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Troubleshoot the equipment, make minor repairs and maintenance, write faults and repairs in the logbook, and call maintenance for larger faults.

steps.what: Extrusion operator maintains and makes minor repairs to equipment
Extrusion operator writes faults and repairs in the machine logbook
Extrusion operator phones maintenance about larger faults

tasks.design: Faults and repairs are logged on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with downtime reasons from a pick list and a short note, instead of a paper logbook. Larger faults go to maintenance as a request from the terminal with the machine, fault code and photo, so most need no call. Troubleshooting and repairs stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults were written in a logbook and maintenance was phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems record downtime reasons and send maintenance requests.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent stops still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a screw that is about to seize.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X Machine Monitoring collects machine statuses and assigns them to the workplace.
Downtime logged per operator can observe performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the machine fault to maintenance called; major repairs are outside.
Input contract: terminals at each line; fallback is the logbook and phone.
Maintenance staff read requests as they took calls.

incremental.description: Extrusion operator adds notes for faults without a code.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few faults; high: older lines with frequent small faults.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count material at the machine, record material used on the job sheet, decide when to request more, request material from the warehouse, and store it.

steps.what: Extrusion operator counts material bags and coils at the machine
Extrusion operator writes material used on the job sheet
Extrusion operator decides when to request more material
Extrusion operator requests material from the warehouse by phone
Extrusion operator stores materials and maintains the inventory area

tasks.design: Material is booked to the job by scanning the lot label at the machine in the ERP shop-floor module ({ERP}), so use is not written on the job sheet and the stock at the line stays current; counts become spot checks. The operator calls off more material from the terminal by picking material and quantity, and the warehouse sees the request in its list instead of a phone call. Deciding when to call off and storing material stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material was counted by eye, written on job sheets and requested by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: ERP shop-floor modules book material by scan and take call-offs from the line.
tasks.still_hard: Regrind and part bags have no label.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a batch is damp before it ruins a run.
tasks.altitude: The operator decides call-offs instead of counting and writing.

evidence.claim: Jay Industries reported 86% less inventory variance and 6% higher OEE with Plex MES; vendor case.
Scans tied to an operator login can observe performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to material stored; buying material is outside.
Input contract: lots labelled by the warehouse; fallback is the job sheet and phone.
Call-off decisions stay with the operator.
Warehouse staff read call-offs as they took calls.
research_questions: Do line stops for missing material fall?

incremental.description: Extrusion operator scans each lot used.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much unlabelled regrind; high: all material labelled from the warehouse.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure rod diameter and length, look up the tooling table, select and fit nozzles, spacers and wire guides, and note the tooling used.

steps.what: Extrusion operator measures diameters and lengths of rods
Extrusion operator looks up the tooling table for the diameter on paper
Extrusion operator selects nozzles, spacers and wire guides and fits them
Extrusion operator notes the tooling used on the job sheet

tasks.design: The tooling table per rod diameter and length is held in the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the machine terminal shows the nozzle, spacer and guide sizes for the job, so the operator does not look them up on paper. The tooling used is confirmed on the terminal instead of written on the job sheet. Measuring rods and fitting tooling stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tooling was looked up in paper tables and noted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems hold tooling tables per product.
tasks.still_hard: Worn guides need judgement the table does not give.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a guide is too worn to run another shift.

evidence.claim: Production systems can hold tooling tables per product and show them at the machine.

assumptions: Boundary: from new rods to tooling recorded; tool making is outside.
Input contract: tooling table loaded by the process engineer; fallback is the paper table.

incremental.description: Extrusion operator reports missing table entries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few diameter changes; high: many short runs with different rods.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The extrusion operator keeps setting up, troubleshooting, repairing and fitting tooling; paper job sheets, binders, logbooks and phone requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator with more time on the line.

job.title: Extruding and Drawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
